subject: Life Skills
title: The Eisenhower Matrix
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Eisenhower Matrix usable.

hook.text: Dwight Eisenhower ran a world war and a presidency. He credited one simple grid for keeping him sane.

buildup.text: Draw two axes: urgent vs. not urgent, important vs. not important. Every task falls into one of four boxes.

discovery.text: Urgent and important: do it now. Important but not urgent: schedule it. That second box holds your best work.

twist.text: Most people live in the urgent boxes. Emails, pings, and fires feel productive but crowd out what truly matters.

climax.text: The bottom-right box — not urgent, not important — is where your time quietly disappears. Audit it weekly.

punchline.text: Important rarely screams. Urgent always does.

quiz.question: Which quadrant holds your most valuable work?
